Hi Ben,

Quick heads up: last night’s scheduled bulk inference (nightly-drain-06-01) showed a number of jobs that did not reach finalization within the 4-hour completion window defined in our onboarding SOW. About ~320 out of 12,100 jobs ended in a "PENDING_FINALIZATION" state for >6 hours and required manual re-submits.

This is causing downstream backfills and retail feeds to miss morning cutoffs. We tried automatic retries but saw duplicate artifacts for ~10% of retried jobs. We need:

- A short explanation of root cause (was this a drain, eviction, or queueing issue?)
- A plan for safe retry to avoid duplicates (idempotency guidance)
- Temporary SLA relief / credit for the missed completion window last night

Can you escalate? Procurement is copied — they’ll want the remediation plan and any proposed credit to accept the renewal review next week.

Subject: (internal) Proposed safe-retry + finalization escrow workflow

Ben / Evelyn / Stephanie — quick internal summary and proposal after a fast triage of the logs:

Findings:
- Host decommission triggered during heavy KV-cache warming; the runtime moved ~2.6% of active requests into "handoff" queues handled by warm nodes. Hand-off added ~2.2–3.8s per token which cascaded for long sequences; finalization RPCs timed out in our client ack path rather than server-side commit in some cases.
- Client attempted retries without an idempotency key, so duplicate artifacts were produced when finalization did in fact go through server-side but client didn't receive ack.

Proposal (two-pronged, short + medium-term):
Short-term (quick config + guidance, deployable in 24–36h):
- Escrow-based finalization gate: when a job enters "PENDING_FINALIZATION" > 30m, mark it into a protected escrow state. Auto-retry requests for the same job id will return a 202 + "escrowed" header and include the canonical run_instance_id. Clients should refrain from creating new artifacts until final state returned.
- Require client-supplied idempotency-token ("X-Idempotency-Key"). If absent, Redwood will generate one and return it in headers. Retries with same token will be treated as deduplicated.
- Safe-retry guidance doc (bullet list) to be sent to FastRetail; sample client change is small (rely on run_instance_id + idempotency-key).

Medium-term (policy + runtime):
- Persist finalization ack to a short-lived store (48h) keyed by idempotency-token so late client retries can be reconciled without duplicate artifacts.
- Add a queue-drain policy to stagger warm node handoffs during decommission windows to avoid cascade latencies.

SLA credit suggestion: 1.5% usage credit for the impacted daily window (calculation sheet attached). We should present both a credit and a contractual minor SLA amendment for scheduled host drains.

I can package the short-term config change into a tenant rollout tomorrow if we have sign-off from Ben / Sales and legal on the credit ask.

Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Maya — following up with our concrete proposal and next steps. Summary below; attached draft SLA amendment and a short safe-retry guidance doc.

What happened (TL;DR): a scheduled decommission overlapped with your heavy nightly-drain run and caused a small percentage of jobs to be handed to warm nodes; some client-side finalization acks were lost, which led clients to retry and create duplicates.

What we’re proposing (agreed next week timeline if acceptable):
1) Short-term tenant config change (48–72h): escrow gating + mandatory idempotency-token headers. This is a non-breaking config — Redwood will return tokens if clients do not supply them.
2) Medium-term (Q3): short-lived finalization ack store (48h) + smarter drain staggering.
3) SLA remediation: one-time 1.5% usage credit for the impacted daily bill; plus a contract amendment that documents a planned maintenance drain carve-out (attached).

Action items for FastRetail:
- Confirm you accept the short-term config change and that your client team can adopt the idempotency-token in the next 48–72h.
- If you accept the amendment, procurement can sign via DocuSign (link below) and we’ll schedule the tenant rollout.
